Winter left Inter for his former club Ajax in 1999. In 2001, he was loaned out to [Sparta Rotterdam](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Sparta_Rotterdam "Sparta Rotterdam"). He played 32 games for Sparta Rotterdam and scored one goal before returning to Ajax to finish his career, and where he chose to retire in 2003.

Winter began his career with amateur club VV Unicum in [Lelystad](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Lelystad "Lelystad"), moved on to SV Lelystad, and the same year joined [Ajax](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/AFC_Ajax "AFC Ajax") at the age of 19. His first game for Ajax was a match against [FC Utrecht](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/FC_Utrecht "FC Utrecht") on 6 April 1986, which Ajax won 3–0. Winter won two [KNVB Cups](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/KNVB_Cup "KNVB Cup") (1987 and 1988), the [Eredivisie](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/Eredivisie "Eredivisie") title (1990), the [European Cup Winners' Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1986%E2%80%9387_European_Cup_Winners'_Cup "1986–87 European Cup Winners' Cup") (1987) and the [UEFA Cup](https://en.wikipedia.org/wiki/1991%E2%80%9392_UEFA_Cup "1991–92 UEFA Cup") (1992).

notes: Ajax first-team debut was 6 April 1986. Retains the 1999 Ajax playing return and 2001–2002 Sparta Rotterdam loan. The 2003 endpoint is retirement/contract end, not a claim of appearances that year: NFT ends with Sparta in 2001/02 and Ajax league appearances in the second spell are all in 1999/00–2000/01. No extra Ajax node is inserted for the unused post-loan registration. Youth and managerial clubs excluded.

Marc broke into the first team in 1991, playing less than a dozen games in the second tier before moving to Eredivisie outfit Willem II. Before long, Overmars was winning the Champions League with Ajax, scoring the winner at Old Trafford for Arsenal and strutting his stuff at Camp Nou. At his peak, he was rightly regarded as one of the world’s best wingers.

His route into Quick Boys' first team came about through circumstance: in early 1998, first-team striker Pieter Slootweg announced his intention to join rivals VV Katwijk, making him unwelcome at the club and leaving a vacancy in attack. Kuyt, then an under-19 player, was given his chance; Quick Boys won the remaining six matches of the Hoofdklasse season, with Kuyt contributing three goals.[10]

Kuyt announced his retirement from professional football in 2017, having scored a hat-trick in the final game of the season to secure Feyenoord their first Eredivisie title since 1999 three days earlier. He briefly came out of retirement the following April, to help out Quick Boys, where he already was the assistant-manager, to fix their shortage on strikers for the remainder of the season.[8]
